title: The Benyuan Dharma Gate Is an Outer Path Attached to Buddhism
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Q: Is the Benyuan Dharma Gate an outer path attached to Buddhism?

inline.s: Q: Is the Benyuan Dharma Gate an outer path attached to Buddhism?

A: The Benyuan Dharma Gate is, of course, an outer path attached to Buddhism. What is meant by an outer path attached to Buddhism is one that appropriates Buddhism while distorting and tampering with Buddhist doctrine.

It exploits weaknesses of human nature among the faithful — such as shrinking from difficulty, taking shortcuts, and clinging to worldly pleasures — to fool the faithful and cheat them of fame and profit,
and even to attain a certain political end.
The Benyuan Dharma Gate fully fits this definition, and is therefore a genuine, out-and-out outer path attached to Buddhism.
Ordinary outer paths attached to Buddhism act under the banner of the Dharma,
fooling the faithful
in order to cheat them of fame and wealth, and even to attain a certain political end.
But the Benyuan Dharma Gate goes far beyond this:
it seeks to destroy the true Dharma of the Buddha from its very roots.
So in addition to a systematic false teaching that distorts and tampers with Buddhist doctrine, it also instigates the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil in order to wreck the sangha.
And through the so-called
“Triple Abolition and Establishment”
(see
“Appendix Five: The Triple Abolition and Establishment of the Benyuan Dharma Gate”
it carries out the slaughter of those who differ from it, in order to do away with the true Dharma. This is where the enormous harmfulness of the Benyuan Dharma Gate lies!

According to the Benyuan Dharma Gate’s topsy-turvy teaching, its instigation of breaking precepts and doing evil, and its scheming to wipe out opponents, while it abolishes the whole Path of Sagely Practice
(every path other than the Pure Land Dharma Gate)

, it will also slander the earnestly concentrated Buddha-recitation that accords with the teaching as “self-power recitation” and abolish it. At that point the Buddhist fold becomes a single unified world for those who neither earnestly and single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name, nor keep the precepts, nor cultivate merit, nor purify their own minds, and who may even do evil for their whole lives. Monks who eat meat and keep wives no longer shave their heads, and even the monk’s robe is set aside out of fear of public scrutiny when they break precepts and do evil. In this way the true sangha that serves as the model for gods and men no longer exists, and the masses, unable to obtain the genuine Dharma and finding no fruit from their practice, lose faith in the Dharma. What a scene this is!
(This scene already has precedent; see
The Practice of the Teaching of Master Hōnen
When the cart ahead overturns, the cart behind takes warning!
[When the cart ahead overturns, the cart behind takes warning] When the cart in front overturns, the cart behind must take warning from it.
Q: Why must the Benyuan Dharma Gate be criticized?
A: Because the actions of the Benyuan Dharma Gate possess the three great characteristics of
destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha
. First,
topsy-turvy teaching
, replacing the true Dharma with a false one

(they boast loudly that rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Utmost Bliss requires no “cutting off evil and doing good,” no “keeping the precepts,” that “doing evil and committing crimes do not matter,” that “the evil person is the true capacity whom Amitābha Buddha saves,” that “reciting the name surely brings rebirth,” that “the gate of the great vow,” and so on — see the several appendices and the further reading.)
. Second,
instigating the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil

, corrupting the fourfold assembly of home-leavers and householders, and in particular seeking to destroy the true sangha that is the model for gods and men, so as to extinguish the Buddha’s true Dharma
(see the several appendices)
The Buddha said:
“In the future the destruction of the true Dharma will not come from the assault of the demons and heretics, but precisely from the corruption and collapse of the sangha!”
(On the Sangha Jewel)
Third, the slaughter of those who differ and the monopolization of all under heaven
(see the section
“Triple Abolition and Establishment”
in the appendix)
making the Buddhist fold a single unified world of false teachings and evil persons.
In this way, the true Dharma of the Buddha is destroyed.
And the retribution for destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha is most dreadful:
whether the propagators of the Benyuan Dharma Gate, or their followers, supporters, and patrons
(the karmic guilt of the latter three kinds of persons is that of helping the tiger to do mischief)
all of them will fall into the Avīci hell for long kalpas.
So whether for the sake of defending the true Dharma, or out of compassion, one must criticize the Benyuan Dharma Gate,
and let everyone know the truth.

(Those who deliberately do evil certainly deserve their retribution; but those faithful who are fooled and mistakenly board a pirate ship, and who in a confused way follow them in creating karmic evil
(destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha)
and receiving retribution
(falling into the Avīci hell for long kalpas)
, are truly pitiable and hardly worth it. O vast and boundless heaven, what kind of men are these!)

In the Buddha Treasury Sutra, in the chapter on ancient times, the seventh, the Buddha, in speaking of the retribution of those who in the past destroyed the true Dharma of the Buddha and of their followers, supporters, and patrons, says:
These evil persons,
destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha,

also bring great ruin and affliction to many people. Moreover, after those evil persons die, they fall into the Avīci hell, lying supine for nine hundred trillion years, lying prone for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the left side
(lying on the left side)
for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the right side
(lying on the right side)
for nine hundred trillion years, burning and charred
(‘consume’ — that is, scorched)

upon the hot iron. Dying there, they are reborn in the roasting hell, the great roasting hell, the living hell, and the black-rope hell, experiencing all such suffering for the same number of years as above. Dying in the black-rope hell, they are reborn again in the great Avīci hell.
Śāriputra,
for this reason, whether householders or home-leavers who draw near to such a person
(the followers of these evil persons)
, and the good teachers
(good knowing companions, i.e., the supporters of these evil persons)
and all the patrons
(the benefactors and patrons of these evil persons)
, all told six hundred forty trillion persons, together with these four teachers
(with these four evil persons)
live and die together, and in the great hell undergo all manner of burning and boiling.
Thus, Śāriputra,
all the good-teacher households of such a person, all the patron households, disciples, teachers, and those who follow along — all who are counted in that number are born in hell.

Śāriputra, you cannot know their number; only the Tathāgata can know it. Those who with these evil persons fall into the great hell, living and dying together, number in all six hundred forty trillion persons; thus they revolve and suffer for one kalpa, dwelling in hell until the conflagration of the great kalpa. Why is this? Śāriputra, to break the utmost, right, and perfect enlightenment of the Tathāgatas is a very heavy offense and not a light one. When the great kalpa burns, these four evil persons and the six hundred forty trillion persons pass from this Avīci great hell and are reborn elsewhere, in the great hell. Why? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses being complete, their retribution is not small: in another place, for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of na-yuta years they undergo great suffering. When the world is produced again, these four evil persons and the six hundred forty trillion persons, together with the others whose offenses are not yet finished, at their death are reborn again in the great hell of this world.”

(Translation: These evil persons, destroying the true Dharma of the Buddha, also cause many who follow them to suffer great distress. Moreover, after these evil persons die, they fall into the Avīci hell, lying supine on the hot iron for nine hundred trillion years, lying prone for nine hundred trillion years, lying on the left side for nine hundred trillion years, and lying on the right side for nine hundred trillion years, burning and charred in the Avīci hell. After dying in the Avīci hell, they are reborn in the roasting hell, the great roasting hell, the living hell, and the black-rope hell, in each of which in turn they undergo the manifold suffering of lying supine nine hundred trillion years, prone nine hundred trillion years, on the left side nine hundred trillion years, and on the right side nine hundred trillion years. Finally, dying in the black-rope hell, they are reborn again into the great Avīci hell to continue their suffering. Śāriputra, for this reason, all householders and home-leavers who draw near to these four evil monks, and their close associates (good teachers), and their patrons (benefactors), six hundred forty trillion persons in all, live and die together with the four evil monks, fall together into hell, and undergo all manner of burning and boiling in the great hell. Thus, Śāriputra, all the supporters of these four evil monks, the households of all the patrons (benefactors), the disciples, the teachers, and those who follow along — all who are counted in that number are born in hell. Śāriputra, you cannot know how many there are; only the Tathāgata can know. Those who with these four evil monks fall into the great hell, living and dying together, number in all six hundred forty trillion persons; thus they revolve and suffer for one great kalpa, remaining in hell until the conflagration of the kalpa. Why? Śāriputra, they break the utmost, right, and perfect enlightenment of the Buddhas — an offense very heavy, not light. If at the end of a corrupt kalpa the conflagration burns, these four evil monks and those six hundred forty trillion persons pass from this Avīci great hell and are reborn in great hells elsewhere. Why? Śāriputra, their heavy offenses being complete, their retribution is not small: in the great hells of other regions for countless hundreds of thousands of billions of na-yuta years they undergo great suffering. When this world is produced again, these four evil monks and the six hundred forty trillion persons, together with those others whose offenses are not yet complete, at their death are reborn again into the great hell of this world.)
[Helping the tiger to do mischief (
chang

)] To serve as the tiger’s ghost helper. In old legends, a person eaten by a tiger becomes a ghost helper, whose sole task is to lure people to be eaten by the tiger. [One kalpa] Here this refers to one great kalpa. A great kalpa comprises the four intermediate kalpas of formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness. At the end of the kalpa of destruction there necessarily arise the flood, fire, and wind calamities.

blocks.text: Appendix One: This Undercurrent That the Buddhist Community Ought to Take Seriously

inline.s: Master Weixian

[Master Weixian] A native of Pengxi, Sichuan, he entered the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Academy at age fourteen and was highly regarded by Master Taixu, his Buddhist scholarship being profound. When young, in his practice he produced essays and works that made his name known in Buddhist circles. In the 1950s he was buffeted by political movements and imprisoned for twenty-six years, enduring great hardship behind bars. In prison he practiced diligently without cease and studied the Buddhist canon deeply. On his release in the 1980s he became the abbot of Chongqing Ciyun Temple, widely spreading the good karma of the Dharma. With his profound learning he taught the Dharma and transmitted the precepts at monasteries at home and abroad, earning deep reverence throughout the Buddhist world. He served as chairman of the advisory committee of the Buddhist Association of China, president of the Chongqing Buddhist Association, and head of the Chongqing Buddhist Academy. He passed away at Tushan Temple in Nanan district, Chongqing, at 4:50 a.m. on February 2, 2013, at the age of ninety-three.
[Editor’s note] This essay reveals that China’s Benyuan Dharma Gate, whether in doctrine or in funding, all derives from the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate,
and is a branch center of the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate:
More and more evidence shows that the impact of this undercurrent is by no means accidental or spontaneous,
but organized and planned,
backed both by
huge sums of money
, and possessing channels and nodes for
distributing books and recorded tapes
, and moreover possessing those who
preach and stir up zeal, monks, nuns, and laymen alike.
About two years ago (that is, 1997),
the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate contacted temples in Jiangxi; if a large ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ center could be built, they could remit ten million yuan.
These
‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ centers

established with funding from the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate, because the name ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ is too notorious, now change their signboards to ‘relying on Master Shandao,’ ‘promoting Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought,’ ‘promoting Master Shandao’s Buddha-recitation Dharma Gate,’ and the ‘Shandao school,’ and try as far as possible to conceal their relation to the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate. These people, harboring a crooked heart and practicing deceit, think that everyone can be cheated and that there is no one in the world wiser than they —
(there is no one in the world cleverer than me)
—not realizing that evil retribution lies behind, coming one after another.
Master Shandao taught: “What has come is true; what is sincere is real. To make clear that all beings’ practice and understanding in body, speech, and mind,
must be done with a genuine mind.

One must not outwardly display a virtuous and diligent appearance while inwardly harboring falsehood — greed, hatred, perversity, deceit, all manner of cunning — an evil nature hard to touch, a matter like venomous snakes and scorpions. Though one sets body, speech, and mind in motion, it is called the goodness of mixed poison, and also called practice of falsehood, not genuine karma. If one settles the mind and practices in this way, then even if one toils body and mind, day and night through the twelve hours, rushing and working as though one’s head were on fire, all of it is
(with ‘all’ meaning ‘altogether’)
called the goodness of mixed poison.
To wish to turn back from this mixed-poison practice and seek rebirth in that Buddha’s Pure Land is altogether impossible.
” (The Four-Part Commentary on the Contemplation Sutra)

[It is a branch center of the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate] Master Jingkong’s Questions and Answers on Buddhist Study, in answer to the seventy-fourth session with fellow practitioners in Hong Kong, contains this: “Q:
Recently a home-leaver has been preaching the Dharma in various places in China, and is in fact promoting a heresy — the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate
Their practice is this: if a monastery is willing to publicize the Japanese Jōdo Shinshū for them, they invest ten million renminbi at a stroke.
Second,
if a Chinese layman is willing to publicize the Jōdo Shinshū for them online, they can supply a monthly salary and bonus.

The concrete way of working is that the Chinese layman comes forward to establish a forum and assigns someone every day to repost Japanese Jōdo Shinshū posts on the major Pure Land forums. If this Chinese layman is very rich in Buddhist knowledge, they can supply a monthly salary of ten thousand renminbi (note: the layman’s monthly salary is ten thousand renminbi; if he is a Dharma master, how much monthly salary do they supply?)

. The Japanese demand is that this seller of Buddhism should pretend to be a devoted disciple of Master Yinguang, Master Jingkong, or a Tantric guru, mix with ordinary Buddhist friends online, so that everyone admires their Buddhist grounding, and then lead these ordinary friends to accept the views of Japanese Jōdo Shinshū. I ask the Elder Master to instruct on the above matters.”

[Honganji] Honganji is the head temple of the Jōdo Shinshū Honganji school of Japanese Buddhism. [Jōdo Shinshū] Also called the Benyuan school, it permits monks to take wives and have children, and propagates the ‘name-recitation surely brings rebirth, the evil person is the true capacity’ Benyuan Dharma Gate.
Lately, from Buddhist publications and from actual contact, there is reflected
an undercurrent in China’s Buddhist community of ‘studying Japanese Buddhism and taking the Japanese Buddhist road.’
This undercurrent strikes in two directions. First, it destroys the fundamental rule of China’s Han Buddhism that monks must wear the robe, be vegetarian, and remain celibate.

A fair number of Japanese home-leavers take wives and bear children, drink alcohol and eat meat, wear Western suits, and disregard the precepts — which pleases our own monks who do not keep the precepts.
The essay The Alarm Bell (published in Taizhou Buddhism,
, no.
, issue no.
) exposes: “It is now found that in four key temples of City
W

three or four young home-leavers have returned to lay life, and the head of the fairly well-known ‘Kairu Sutra-Printing Society’ — the monk Kairu of Mount Jiuhua — returned to lay life again last year.” It is reported that
in some cities along our coast monks stay at the temple by day, then return to their own private homes to live a family life by night,
and the social impact is extremely bad.
The second direction of impact is
the propagation of Japan’s ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’
, seeking to interfere with and destroy it spiritually and in the direction and path of Buddhist study and practice. The importation of Japanese Buddhism into China is long-standing;
in the 1930s it served the war of aggression against China.

The essay The Alarm Bell discloses that at that time in Wuhu, Anhui, “in Central Second Street there was a Japanese Buddhist temple, with Japanese-style lanterns hanging at the gate bearing the red characters ‘Higashi Honganji,’ and inside lived a Japanese monk and his whole family. The Japanese monk often held a leather drum and walked through the streets beating it. It is said that every city occupied by Japan had such, and that they served with the army, specializing in rites for the dead Japanese soldiers.”

“At that time Japan invaded China. They called it the ‘holy war,’ and killing for the ‘holy war’ was without guilt, and the dead souls passed beyond to the Buddha-land. The glorious names of those who killed many Chinese and had merit could enter the shrine. After the War of Resistance ended, the unpopular Japanese Buddhism vanished from mainland China.”
“Who would have thought that this specter has been resurrected by ‘a certain group of people
(namely Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others)
—is that not absurd?”
The Shanghai layman Zheng Songying, in the essay Destroying the Heterodox and Revealing the Right, Eliminating the Three Harms published in Taizhou Buddhism, points out: “Japan
’s ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ has recently been transmitted to China.
It looks like a Pure Land sect, yet it entirely contravenes the Dharma, misleads living beings, and does great harm;
it is in fact a demon within the teaching!

It claims that so long as one hears the name of Amitābha Buddha and can give rise to faith, one has obtained the ‘identity card’ for the Land of Utmost Bliss, and will definitely be reborn there! No more reciting the Buddha’s name and cultivating; no matter how one dies, without the deathbed assistance of recitation, one will definitely be reborn!” “The ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ requires only a single ‘faith’ and no ‘practice’ at all, relying entirely on other-power and not on self-power — is this still Buddhism?” In fact, in the late Qing and early Republic, the layman Yang Renshan, through the Japanese Buddhist scholar Nanjō Bun’yū, imported a great many Buddhist texts, and with regard to the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ he already criticized and rejected it. (See the Clarification of the Teaching, twelve kinds compiled by the layman Yang, in the Continued Canon.)
No master of China’s modern and contemporary Pure Land school has ever advocated the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate.’
More and more evidence shows that
the impact of this undercurrent is by no means accidental or spontaneous,
but organized and planned,
backed both by
huge sums of money,
and possessing channels and nodes for
distributing books and recording tapes,
and moreover possessing those who
preach and stir up zeal, monks, nuns, and laymen alike.
About two years ago,
the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate contacted temples in Jiangxi; if a large ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ center could be built, they could remit ten million yuan.

At that time they also had doubts about the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ claim that only a single ‘faith’ is needed and one may dispense with reciting the Buddha’s name and practice. But they were again tempted to use this huge sum to build a center and in the future still propagate the pure and correct Pure Land school, and wrote to ask the Shanghai elder layman Zheng Songying. The elder Zheng’s reply pointed out: “To do so is to set a wrong ground and should be firmly rejected and not accepted.” Only then did they desist.
It is now found that the nodes propagating the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ are very many; those very active, of which there are several.
The essay The Alarm Bell says: “In the past two years, the
Japanese Jōdo Shinshū Benyuan Dharma Gate
has repeatedly mailed books and propagandist materials and so on to various Buddhist institutions in Anhui, and some Buddhists have already been affected.”
There are two young home-leavers who call themselves of Mount Jiuhua, propagating Japanese Buddhism in various cities; one of them, eloquent, is called ‘Holy Su master’ (
now renamed Master Jingzong, having gone to take refuge with Master Huijing of Taiwan, who advocates the Benyuan Dharma Gate
); they exploit people’s reverence for the sacred site of Mount Jiuhua and respect for its monks, find contacts to help them arrange venues for preaching,
pleasing the inexperienced devout householders and the home-leavers who do not keep the precepts.
This Spring Festival, the two monks Holy Su and another accompanied a Taiwanese nun down from the mountain to preach. From Xuancheng to Wuhu they gave one day’s preaching and one day’s discussion,
and afterward were called to account by the municipal CPPCC and the religious affairs bureau.
In the first half of
, this undercurrent again extended deep into the southwest, and was felt most strongly in particular in Chongqing Municipality. Not only did the Cangtangyan

in Xuancheng, Anhui, and the ‘Ciyuan Group Bodhi Monastery Gift Center’ of Dezhou, Shandong, send in bulk books such as the Amitābha Calling series, but in the summer also a young monk was sent to the Chongqing urban district, very secretly, without revealing his original temple or Dharma name, lodging in the home of a layman and organizing group after group of the faithful to hear him advocate the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate.’ Those deluded grew day by day, until the laymen practicing the Pure Land Dharma Gate in Chongqing were split into two factions. Some lay upholders of the Pure Land ‘two powers’ (Buddha-power and self-power) Dharma Gate raised many questions to this monk, but his answers were not clear, and he even said angrily, “You will fall into hell! Fall into hell! Fall into hell!”
Judging from the above circumstances, if this undercurrent is allowed to spread and grow, it will severely corrode, and even destroy, the entire Buddhist teaching.

(Original editor’s note: The Benyuan Dharma Gate distorts the three Pure Land sutras and one treatise, advocating the needlessness of reciting sutras, keeping precepts, giving rise to bodhicitta, or practicing the six perfections and ten thousand practices of a bodhisattva. This entirely contravenes Buddhist doctrine and the Mahāyāna spirit of transcending the world while being in the world;
it is in reality an
outer path attached to Buddhism
, and should arouse the high regard of and be resisted by the whole Buddhist community. It is also hoped that the government departments concerned pay attention

blocks.text: Appendix Two: Guard Against the Harm and the Misleading of the Benyuan Dharma Gate to the Pure Land School

inline.s: [Original editor’s note]

The essay Guarding Against the Harm and the Misleading of the Benyuan Dharma Gate to the Pure Land School, in the magazine Sound of the Dharma, the journal of the Buddhist Association of China, lists many false teachings of the Benyuan Dharma Gate, and finally warns that “if its theory is allowed to circulate in the Buddhist community, it will have a destructive influence on the abiding of the true Dharma.”

blocks.text: 1. A Brief Account of the Origin and Development of the Benyuan Dharma Gate

inline.s: The theory of the Benyuan Dharma Gate originated with the Japanese master Hōnen, and reached its summit with his disciple Shinran.

As the essay in the Sound of the Dharma says, “its basic theory single-mindedly emphasizes other-power, and is in many places inconsistent with the sutras and treatises.” Yang Renshan, the father of the revival of Chinese Buddhism, in his Critique of the Selected Collection on the Original Vow Recitation says, “I find that this collection is inconsistent with the sutras’ meaning in quite a number of places,” and in his Critique of the Shinshū Doctrine says, “I find it is inconsistent with the sutras’ meaning in quite a number of places,”
and criticizes their false teaching as “
hiding the machinery of the destruction of the Dharma
Master Hōnen’s theory had already deviated from Master Shandao, and the Jōdo Shinshū (Benyuan Dharma Gate) founded by his disciple Master Shinran was even further from Master Shandao.
Master Shandao’s thought was “even the evil person is reborn, how much more the good person”; but in Jōdo Shinshū it became the ‘evil person is the true capacity’ doctrine of “
even the good person is reborn, how much more the evil person”!
The ‘even ten recitations’ of the eighteenth vow is also construed by the Benyuan Dharma Gate as “so long as one deeply believes in Amitābha’s original vow (the eighteenth vow),
one recitation is rebirth in the reward land

, and one immediately attains Buddhahood, transcending the nine grades. So there is no need for many recitations; otherwise it is not trusting Amitābha’s original vow, and so recitation is only a deed of gratitude.”
(One of the characteristics of the Benyuan Dharma Gate: topsy-turvy teaching.)

Therefore, even Master Hōnen himself rebuked Shinran as “an outer path attached to the Buddha’s teaching, a follower of the demon horde, destroying the Buddha’s Dharma, an outer path beyond the outer paths,” and warned the multitude, “Be careful not to follow that false teaching.”
But up to the present day, these false teachings that even Hōnen had rebuked
have been inherited by Master Huijing and others, who propagate the Benyuan Dharma Gate under the banner of the ‘Shandao school’.
Master Huijing’s The Essence of Master Shandao says: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to display Amitābha’s original vow:
the evil person is the true capacity
The Benyuan Dharma Gate is that the evil person is the true capacity

—other-power, faith and practice, rebirth in the reward land. That is, the most evil and lowest person, depending on the most excellent and highest Dharma, is born in the highest and most wondrous land.”
Note:
The Sutra of the Buddha’s Praise of the Pure Land, which our teacher Śākyamuni Buddha proclaimed with his golden mouth, praising the Pure Land that Amitābha Buddha extols and receives, says:
“Sentient beings of little root of good are not those who can attain rebirth in the pure Buddha-land of the Land of Utmost Bliss of Amitāyus.
(Translation: sentient beings with little root of good (the good of body, speech, and mind) cannot attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. See
Annotation on the Sutra of the Buddha’s Praise of the Pure Land

Yet the Benyuan Dharma Gate loudly advocates the evil-person-is-the-true-capacity doctrine, making Amitābha Buddha’s great vow into a protective umbrella for the evil person. Such slandering of the Buddha and destruction of the Dharma goes to this very extreme!
In the Contemplation Sutra of Infinite Life, the person of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds is not one who is reborn just by reciting the name;
rather, he attains rebirth by accomplishing the continuous ten recitations at the moment of death, extinguishing his offenses
(see
Annotation on the Lowest Grade and Lowest Birth Section of the Contemplation Sutra
. Originally, the ‘lowest grade and lowest birth section’ of the Contemplation Sutra is about the grade of such a reborn person
(the person of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds who, by accomplishing the continuous ten recitations at death, extinguishes offenses and is reborn)
, which is the lowest grade and lowest birth; but the Benyuan Dharma Gate deliberately omits
the key of ‘ten continuous recitations at the moment of death’

, exaggerating it to the point that all persons of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds who merely recite the Buddha’s name once are reborn, and even advocating the so-called evil-person-is-the-true-capacity doctrine
(Amitābha’s saving has the evil person as its true capacity)

Moreover, even those who are said in the sutra to attain rebirth despite the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds did so because in past lives they had deeply planted good roots and once sown the seed of bodhi. Master Ouyi
says
“The sutra says that those who commit the ten evil deeds and five heinous offenses yet attain rebirth
must have planted the seed of bodhi in the past.
Without the seed of bodhi, how could they meet a good friend? Even if they met a good friend who urged them on, how could they at once give rise to faith and vow and recite the great name?”
(The Spiritual Peak Collected Writings, General Sermon at the Tianma Monastery of Shepu)
